Updating the API Conventions Reference

Two new rows for the status-code table Lesson 3 started — the written convention doc keeps growing alongside the code.

Lesson 3's API Conventions Reference slide promised that "any new endpoint added later in this build is expected to fit into this same table rather than inventing its own response shape" — this lesson is the first test of that promise, and it holds up cleanly: nothing about the response envelope ({ data }/{ data, meta }/{ error }) or how errors reach the client changed at all. What's new is two rows the status-code table didn't need until routes could be protected at all:

Situation Status
No valid proof of who's making the request (authenticate) 401 Unauthorized
Authenticated, but this role can never perform this action (authorize) 403 Forbidden

Both still go through the exact same { error: { message } } shape as every other error in this project (Lesson 3) — ApiError(401, ...) and ApiError(403, ...), thrown from authenticate.js/authorize.js and caught by the same centralized errorHandler.js as everything else. The one thing worth being precise about, alongside the table: this lesson's scoped 404s (previous two slides) aren't a third new status — 404 was already in Lesson 3's table for "the URL names something that doesn't exist." What changed is only what counts as not existing, now that "doesn't exist" and "exists, but isn't visible to you" resolve to the exact same response.
